title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act requires companies that develop or deploy artificial intelligence to evaluate and reduce the environmental impacts of their AI systems, such as energy use and carbon emissions. It establishes reporting, certification, and compliance rules to ensure AI technologies meet sustainability standards and protect the environment.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a proposed law that limits the use of artificial intelligence in medical settings, requiring that diagnoses and treatment plans be made by licensed doctors rather than AI systems. The bill aims to protect patient safety, maintain professional accountability, and ensure that only qualified medical practitioners are responsible for direct patient care.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act aims to encourage the export of AI technologies and related components. It likely introduces incentives and regulatory measures to help domestic companies ship AI hardware, software, and services abroad, thereby boosting the national AI ecosystem and global competitiveness.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act aims to promote transparency and collaboration in AI development by encouraging the use of open‑source tools and datasets. It establishes guidelines for sharing code, fostering innovation, and ensuring that AI technologies remain accessible and accountable to the public.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is designed to protect veterans by regulating how artificial intelligence is used in services and benefits that affect them. It will establish clear guidelines for transparency, safety, and accountability in AI systems that support or impact veterans’ health, welfare, and rights.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a proposed law designed to set clear rules and guidelines that help protect society from potential risks posed by advanced artificial intelligence. It encourages collaboration between government, businesses, and researchers to identify threats, develop safeguards, and ensure AI systems are safe and reliable before they are widely deployed.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 aims to reduce unfair outcomes in AI by requiring companies to audit their models for bias, disclose the data they use, and give people a way to challenge decisions that affect them. It also sets up a regulator to oversee compliance and enforce penalties on firms that don’t meet these new standards.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 seeks to protect AI developers by creating stronger legal safeguards against unauthorized copying and distribution of AI models. It establishes penalties and enforcement mechanisms to deter theft and ensures that intellectual property rights for AI technologies are respected across the United States.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies that deploy AI and algorithmic systems to assess how those systems affect privacy, fairness, and public safety. It mandates regular audits, risk assessments, and transparency reports so that consumers are protected from biased or harmful automated decisions.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act sets requirements to ensure that artificial intelligence systems used in defense are dependable, safe, and meet specified performance standards. It also mandates detailed reporting on AI deployments, incidents, and compliance to promote transparency and accountability within defense AI operations.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed piece of legislation aimed at enhancing oversight and regulation of artificial intelligence. It seeks to promote safety, transparency, and accountability in the development and use of AI technologies.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires the government to publish an annual report that details how artificial intelligence is being developed, deployed, and regulated across the country. The act also sets guidelines for transparency, data security, and ethical use of AI to monitor its impact on society and the economy.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard the integrity of elections by banning the use of AI-generated content that could mislead or manipulate voters. It requires transparency about AI use in political messaging and sets up enforcement mechanisms to hold parties accountable for deceptive practices.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires companies to closely watch and report on AI systems that can improve themselves without external help. It aims to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability by mandating oversight and safeguards for these autonomous improvements.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt to the construction of new data centers used for artificial intelligence. It aims to address concerns about environmental impact and resource use until more sustainable practices are developed.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The act seeks to protect families from the rising energy costs associated with large AI data centers. It proposes measures such as regulating power usage, encouraging renewable energy adoption, and providing financial relief to households affected by high utility bills.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes to pause or restrict the construction and operation of new data centers specifically for AI applications. It aims to address concerns about environmental impact, resource consumption, and data security associated with large AI infrastructure.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 34 - 1.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed legislation aimed at regulating artificial intelligence to ensure safety, fairness, and accountability. It seeks to establish standards and oversight mechanisms to mitigate risks and promote responsible AI use.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: This act aims to regulate the safety of AI-powered toys for children, setting standards for design, data privacy, and content. It establishes oversight, testing, and enforcement to protect children from harmful or inappropriate AI behavior in toys.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is designed to protect children and teens from having their personal information collected or used by artificial intelligence without appropriate safeguards. The law requires that AI developers obtain parental permission, provide clear privacy notices, and limit the amount of data that can be stored or shared about minors.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is a proposed law that would require Chinese companies and research institutions to regularly report on how they develop, use, and oversee AI technologies. The goal is to increase transparency, accountability, and safety by setting reporting standards and creating oversight mechanisms that can impose penalties for non‑compliance.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act establishes rules to make AI models more understandable and transparent. It requires companies to publish clear documentation and accessible explanations of how their models work so that users and regulators can review and assess their behavior.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill proposes a framework to deliver “functional bills of materials” for artificial intelligence systems, which would detail the components, data, and processes used to build and operate those systems. It also includes other provisions aimed at improving transparency, accountability, and regulatory oversight for AI development and deployment.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act aims to build a skilled workforce that can responsibly develop and oversee AI technologies, ensuring that they are safe, ethical, and transparent. It proposes training programs, certification standards, and workforce development initiatives to support experts who can foster public trust in AI systems.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to prevent AI companies from charging excessively high prices for their services and from fixing or manipulating wages for workers in the industry. It seeks to promote fair pricing and protect employees from discriminatory labor practices.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 establishes guidelines for the development, deployment, and oversight of artificial intelligence systems used in the agricultural sector. It aims to ensure AI technologies enhance farm productivity while safeguarding farmers' privacy, safety, and economic interests.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: This act encourages the use of AI in the financial sector by providing regulatory support and incentives, aiming to boost innovation and competitiveness. It establishes guidelines for responsible AI deployment and safeguards for consumer protection while promoting transparency and ethical standards.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: This act aims to accelerate the adoption of AI technologies in financial services by streamlining regulations and encouraging innovation across the industry. It also establishes safeguards to protect consumers, ensure data security, and maintain overall market stability.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act is a legislative initiative aimed at cultivating a strong workforce in the AI field. It proposes programs and incentives to attract, train, and retain skilled professionals, thereby boosting innovation and ensuring the country stays competitive in artificial intelligence.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act prohibits the establishment or operation of AI data centers on land owned or managed by the federal government. This measure aims to restrict the expansion of AI infrastructure on federal properties, protecting national resources and ensuring responsible use of government land.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to give students and teachers the knowledge and skills needed to use AI safely and responsibly, by setting clear curriculum standards and training requirements. It also allocates resources and guidance so schools can integrate AI tools equitably, promoting digital citizenship and preparing students for an AI‑driven future.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to embed AI education into elementary and high school curricula so that students can navigate a world increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence. It sets out standards, resources, and training for teachers to teach AI concepts, ensuring learners understand both its benefits and potential risks.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a new law that establishes comprehensive rules for developing, deploying, and using artificial intelligence. It focuses on making AI systems safe, transparent, and accountable while protecting privacy, promoting fairness, and encouraging responsible innovation across the economy.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act is designed to help schools incorporate artificial intelligence tools responsibly and effectively. It provides guidelines for teachers and students, ensuring safe use, privacy protection, and AI education across the curriculum.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives believes that all Americans and communities affected by AI data center projects deserve transparency about those projects. They also want these communities to have local decision‑making power over how the data centers are built or run.
